# Third-party material

## most-metal-printer.jpg

The open-source metal 3-D printer built at Michigan Tech's Open Sustainability
Technology Lab — a MIG welding torch on a RepRap-derived frame, mid-deposition.
**This is their machine, not mine.** It is included because it is what the
planner in this repository targets.

- **Source:** [Appropedia — Open-source metal 3-D printer](https://www.appropedia.org/Open-source_metal_3-D_printer)
  ([file page](https://www.appropedia.org/File:Sparks1.jpg))
- **Uploaded by:** Joshua M. Pearce, 2 December 2013
- **Licence:** GNU Free Documentation License v1.3 — full text in
  [`GFDL-1.3.txt`](GFDL-1.3.txt)
- **Modification:** resized to 1500 px wide; not otherwise altered

The machine and its method are published in:

> G. C. Anzalone, C. Zhang, B. Wijnen, P. G. Sanders and J. M. Pearce,
> "A Low-Cost Open-Source Metal 3-D Printer", *IEEE Access*, vol. 1,
> pp. 803–810, 2013.

The rest of this repository — all source, tests and rendered figures — is MIT
licensed, as stated in the top-level [LICENSE](../../LICENSE). The GFDL applies
to this image only.
